scope: Sargent and Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2 (General States), Chapter 5: ADP Transformations. Conjugate, topologically conjugate and order conjugate dynamical systems (Propositions 5.1.1-5.1.2, Lemma 5.1.3, Examples 5.1.1-5.1.3, Exercises 5.1.1-5.1.3); isomorphic and anti-isomorphic ADPs (Lemma 5.1.4, Theorems 5.1.5-5.1.10, Example 5.1.4, Exercises 5.1.4-5.1.8); Epstein-Zin optimality without irreducibility (Exercises 5.1.9-5.1.11, Lemmas 5.1.11-5.1.12, Proposition 5.1.13) via convexity of the aggregator and Du's theorem for minimization; strong semiconjugacy (Lemmas 5.2.1-5.2.2, Theorems 5.2.3-5.2.4, Exercise 5.2.1) with counterexamples to the one-sided order continuity hypotheses; firm entry (Lemmas 5.2.5-5.2.8, Proposition 5.2.7); factored dynamic programs, order preserving and order reversing (Lemmas 5.2.9-5.2.12, 5.2.15-5.2.17, Theorems 5.2.13 and 5.2.18, Proposition 5.2.14, Exercise 5.2.2); applications to Q-factors (Propositions 5.3.1-5.3.2), structural estimation (Section 5.3.2) and Epstein-Zin savings with iid endowments (Exercises 5.3.1-5.3.2, Algorithm 5.1); with the earlier chapters' models, ADP theory and the Banach lattice bX restated.
source: Thomas J. Sargent and John Stachurski, Dynamic Programming, Volume 2: General States, Chapter 5, pp. 147-182, with the Appendix A results used there.
